findings.gate: Craft Core reader-trust invariant 3 (continuity persistence); DECISIONS row 16, carried into the packet as EXC-B8-CH08-2

draft_evidence.quote: a man in a coat that was not grey sitting on a stool inside the leaves with a book on his knee, who looked at the six of them and the mule as they came under the arch, and counted, and wrote, and did not ask.

comparison_evidence.quote: Six of them on the road, and no mule, because the mule had gone north that morning with a healer's roll on it, and Karis's boxes were on three backs — Brom's, Lira's, his own — and the kit's case on Vastin's

findings.consequence: The crew has no mule. Ch6 closed on Oryn taking it north-west at the fork-stone ('She took the mule's rope. "Millrace."'); Ch7's opening sentence states the new arrangement in as many words; and the r2 packet carries the ruling as an approved exception — EXC-B8-CH08-2, 'the mule went north with Oryn on the 281st; the crew carries the boxes until Millrace (Ch18)' — with DECISIONS row 16 specifying the replacement this chapter is to use: 'Treswick's carter's mule at the trough carries Ch8's beat.' The r2 pass applied that ruling at four of the five places the animal appeared (L9 now 'with the boxes on their backs'; L21 now 'a carter's mule at a trough by the gate'; L27 now 'counted six people and wrote six'; L99 now 'at the four of them') and missed this one. What survives is the worst of the five to keep: it is the crew's own entry under the arch, in the sentence where the city's gate-keeper counts them, so the reader is told the party is six-and-a-mule by the one official who counts — one paragraph after the previous chapter said the mule was gone, and two paragraphs before the same animal is reintroduced as a stranger's at a trough. It also breaks the strength the ruling was protecting: the L23 mule image ('The city had a column for the mule. It was the same column it had for him') only lands if that mule belongs to a carter, and L11 tells the reader it belongs to Cael. Finally, the author report's r2 deviations claim 'no mule in Treswick (planning ruling, row 16) — the carter's mule at the trough carries the beat', which the page does not yet support.
findings.repair_target: ch08.md L11 — cut 'and the mule' from the gate-keeper's sentence, leaving 'who looked at the six of them as they came under the arch, and counted, and wrote, and did not ask.' One phrase; nothing else in the paragraph moves, and the count at the gate then agrees with the innkeeper's count at L27 and the boxes at L9.

findings.gate: Shared Positive Voice §Sentence music; charter §3.1 (the cataloguing narrator's clarity); introduced by the F8 repair

draft_evidence.quote: and Cael understood that she was pricing herself as labour, on purpose, in a city that would have taken her paper and put her on the second tier by noon, and did not know yet which of the two things she was going to be here, and neither did she.

comparison_evidence.quote: ch08.md L91 — keep Lira's two spoken lines and Cael's noticing that she has priced herself; cut the interpretive clause that closes the question ('had decided which of the two things she was going to be here ... and had decided it at the foot of a stair'), leaving the decision live for Ch9.

findings.consequence: The repair is right in substance — the decision is now open, which is what Ch9's want-scene needs — but the new clause is a garden path. 'Cael understood that she was pricing herself ... and did not know yet' offers 'she' as the nearest subject inside the that-clause, and a reader who takes it (most will, since the whole sentence has been about her) then hits 'and neither did she' as a contradiction and has to reparse with Cael as the subject of 'did not know'. The stumble lands on the one sentence in the chapter that Ch9 inherits, and it is a stumble a careful reader hits on first pass, not a real ambiguity of fact.
findings.repair_target: ch08.md L91 — break the subject chain so 'did not know' cannot attach to Lira. E.g. end Cael's reading at 'by noon', then a separate clause naming him: '...put her on the second tier by noon. Which of the two things she was going to be here he did not know, and neither, he thought, did she.' Same content, same openness, one subject per clause.

concerns: The F4 repair CUT the two interpolated beats rather than relocating them, which the r1 repair target offered as the alternative ('relocate ... either before "Do we now?" at L109 or into the permitted narration after L113'). Lost: Karis reading the bluff as strata ('the registry on the old town on the quarry on the crown' — a useful last restatement of the geography the whole chapter has built), and Cael filing her refusal to look at the light. Both are recoverable elsewhere if the planning layer wants them: her strata habit still survives at L9 and L33 ('because a gate was a stratum'), and Cael's own refusal at L103. Contiguity is what the contract required and contiguity is what it now has; recording the loss so a later pass does not think the beats were never written.

L39's added clause is elliptical to the ear: 'a man with no standing a registry could write down and a name a Compact counter might' requires the listener to carry 'write down' across to 'might'. It survives being read aloud and the following clause makes the practical consequence unmistakable ('which made a registry counter the one place in a city he did not go'), so it is not an §8.2 failure — but Seln's standing is the one crew fact the chapter now delivers entirely by implication, and the audio pass should decide whether it wants a verb there.

The chapter's tier vocabulary and the packet's do not obviously agree. The packet's knowledge_boundary lists 'Brom Copper (first tier)' alongside 'Karis unranked by choice (outer district)', while the draft renders Copper as buying 'the outer district and a price for iron and nothing up a stair' (L37) and reserves 'the second tier' for the district above the first wall. The draft's reading is the one STATE_RUNNING's After-Ch9 entry supports (Brom goes up by count, not by tier), so I am not raising it as a contradiction — but the numbering should be pinned in the reference before Ch9's counter scene is rechecked, or the two documents will disagree in the same paragraph.

'A beat.' at L113 is still reproduced from the card as prose. Carried from r1: it is a direction to the author that reads on the page as a stage instruction, and it is the one place in the chapter where the register slips toward script. It survives being read aloud, so it is not an §8.2 failure, but it deserves a decision rather than an inheritance.

'He had lived at the foot of a city once, at fourteen, for a season' (L15) remains unverified. Searched scope: the packet's canon, architecture, DECISIONS, registry, STATE_RUNNING, Ch6, Ch7 and the Book 7 Ch1 reference; method: full-text term scan plus read. If this is new backstory rather than Books 1-3 material, charter §6.4/§11.7 want it flagged and approved rather than minted in passing. Unchanged by the repair, so unchanged as a question.

L9's 'with the boxes on their backs' is collective where the narrator is usually exact: per ch07.md L9 the boxes are on Brom's, Lira's and Cael's backs with the kit's case on Vastin's, and the same sentence individuates Karis 'with the flat'. No reader will mis-count, but STATE_RUNNING's After-Ch9 entry ledgers the boxes person by person, and a cataloguing narrator who says 'their' where he elsewhere says whose is slightly out of register.
The scaffold 'because a man who is going to keep to a place should ___' still runs twice (L17, L49), under the charter §9 cap of three. Unchanged by the repair. A third use in Ch9 would breach.

The author report's deviations array still carries 'Word count ~3,9xx after expansion — in band' as an unresolved self-note, now redundant with the precise word_count field (3931) and the run diagnostics. More materially, the same array asserts 'no mule in Treswick', which finding N1 shows is not yet true on the page; an attestation that outruns the draft is the failure mode the recheck exists to catch.
strengths: The repair discipline is close to exemplary in scope: nine changed lines, every one at a named repair target, no opportunistic rewriting anywhere else in a 3,900-word chapter, and the changes are additive (+19 words) exactly as the r1 word-band concern asked. All eight recorded strengths verify intact.

F2's repair is better than the finding asked for. 'Copper, on paper, which at this gate bought him the outer district and a price for iron and nothing up a stair, and he had not asked for a stair' (L37) does three jobs in one clause — Brom's tier, what the tier buys, and the man's indifference to what it doesn't — and it lands in the going-out inventory's own cadence rather than sitting on top of it.

'on principle and on a count' (L39) is a quiet, exact piece of forward work: it seats Ch9's beat (Seln deliberately kept off the count) inside a sentence about why he avoids counters, without pre-paying anything Ch9 has to earn.

The pass finally has edges — 'a stamped tin on a cord, Brom said, shown at the stair's foot and not taken off' (L45). 'Not taken off' is the detail that makes the object a mechanism rather than a prop: the man who crosses the line wears the line.

Cutting the interpolation restored the close's rhythm. 'Do we now?' / 'Karis looked up the bluff.' / 'A name and a reason' now lands as a three-beat exchange with a held look in the middle, which is what the card designed; the payoff line no longer arrives after a paragraph of interiority the reader has to walk back out of.

The F1 repair kept the beat and spent nothing: 'read her book across the counter, the wrong way round, out of a habit he had thought a winter would cure, and it had not' is, if anything, more physical than the capped phrase it replaces — 'the wrong way round' is the reader's own body at a counter.

The chapter still passes Gate 27 on its own terms rather than by omission: the moral weight sits in what four people decline to use (Vastin's papers, Lira's paper, Cael's road round the bluff, Karis's refusal to hurry the provision), and the book lets each refusal cost something.
